thread:
alex: Heads up — seeing a 99th% latency spike (~450ms token) on serve-pool-A around 15:10 UTC. Correlates with a bunch of KV cache rotation logs when mem usage crosses ~18.5GB.

priya: Can you drop the grafana link and the exact trace id?

alex: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv?panel=3&from=1739876400&to=1739876600 trace=tr_9f2c (saw 3x spikes in 2m)

michael: Quick skim of logs: lots of churn like: `kv:rotate evict=120 policy=FIFO reinserts=0 paged=32`. Looks like FIFO is kicking in hard.

jen: Interesting — recent change to batching heuristics increased avg seq length and we moved some requests to pool-A. Could increase per-request KV pressure.

alex: Also saw this in profiler sampled from the hot host:
```
Top stacks:
  48% futex_wait -> kv_lock -> kv_reclaim
  12% kv_reclaim -> evict_fifobatch
  20% kernel_copy -> gpu_submit (batching path)
```
Mutex contention spiking during evict path.

tao: Could be an LRU vs FIFO correctness edge where reinserts under contention cause ordering flips and extra work. Do we have repro?

alex: Lightweight repro on canary: flood requests with long contexts (~8k tokens) and small working set (~60 entries). FIFO path caused immediate rotation; LRU kept hot entries but introduced heavier mutex hold times. Both caused latency but different shapes.

priya: Any signs of stale/incorrect KV reuse (i.e., wrong cache entry served)?

michael: No correctness corruption observed — queries still returned plausible logits. But we do see more cache misses right after rotation: reuse rate drops from 92%->62% for 10s after a rotation event.

jen: That reuse collapse explains token cost and latency. Might be fragmentation: FIFO evicts in blocks, leaving short-lived gaps; subsequent inserts don't pack well -> extra paging.

alex: I dumped a small snapshot of the index layout (trimmed):
```
# index buckets (live_count / bucket_cap)
bucket0: 32/64
bucket1: 1/64
bucket2: 59/64
bucket3: 0/64  # hole
bucket4: 63/64
```
You can see holes after rotation.

tao: Proposal: add a gated change to eviction that does two things: 1) hysteresis watermarks (evict only to 16GB not 18GB), 2) reinsert-from-evict path uses backoff to avoid immediate reordering. Also add per-batch eviction metrics.

priya: Can we also try short-circuit for requests that hit KV but would cause long mutex hold? i.e., speculative GPU kernel selection that doesn't wait for KV inlining if hold > X ms. Kernel selection could prefer streaming variant.

michael: +1. We should test three toggles on canary: FIFO->LRU, hysteresis to 16GB, and kernel fallback. Run each independently and combined.

alex: I'll open a canary run and attach results. For immediate mitigation, bump mem watermark on pool-A to 20GB (less aggressive eviction) and enable kernel fallback.

jen: Small integration test to add: simulate concurrent evict+reinsert with 64 threads and assert no double-free/ordering inversion. Found a tiny race in reinsertion index path earlier.

tao: I'll write the unit test this afternoon. Also add a microbenchmark that measures reuse-rate after synthetic rotation.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0821 — KV cache rotation latency spike on pool-A. Pager notified.

alex: Thanks. Plan: 1) canary toggles (michael+alex), 2) unit tests (tao), 3) canary telemetry dashboard (priya), 4) short-term watermark bump (jen). Will post results here in ~2h. :thumbsup:

priya: Cool — capture the specific profiler stacks and rotation events for postmortem. If we don't see correctness issues we can iterate on policy.

michael: FYI I saw a related but different pattern on pool-B last week where LRU caused long tail due to lock convoy. Might be we need hybrid policy (LRU for hot lanes, FIFO for bulk).

alex: Agree. For now, canary first. I'll update when runs complete.
